# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

## Overrides

None.

===== 00_general/quality/measurement-scope.md
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and, only when the rule below requires it, one confirming full run.
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes. After each round recompute `scoreAdjusted` for the component from the last full run plus the re-run classes (the classes that were not re-run keep their killed and total counts from the full run) and write the per-class numbers into `docs/03_test-strategy.md`. If the recomputed score is at least 1.0 point above the threshold the gate is met and no full run follows. Only a recomputed score less than 1.0 point above the threshold, or a change to a class outside the re-run set, needs the one confirming full run; its result then replaces the recomputed one.
- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.
===== 00_general/quality/severity-scale.md
# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |
===== 00_general/quality/test-strategy.md
# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.
===== 00_general/security/security-baseline.md
# Security baseline

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 0, 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project. Project requirements (`SR-nn`) and the chosen standard level are in `project/02_design/security-requirements.md`.

## Verification standard by component type

| Component type | Standard | Default level |
|---|---|---|
| Web app, API, service | OWASP ASVS (latest) | Level 1; Level 2 when handling authentication, payments or sensitive personal data |
| Mobile app | OWASP MASVS (latest) | L1 |
| Desktop app, CLI, library | Applicable OWASP ASVS chapters | Level 1 |

## Controls for every project

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | All input is validated on the trusted side (server or core), whatever the client does. |
| SB-02 | Every non-public operation checks authentication and authorization. |
| SB-03 | Credentials are stored only as salted, slow hashes; secrets come from configuration (ES-01, ES-02). |
| SB-04 | Data in transit uses TLS outside the local machine. |
| SB-05 | Output is encoded for its context; queries are parameterised. |
| SB-06 | Public and authentication endpoints are rate limited. |
| SB-07 | Errors and logs expose no internals, secrets or personal data (ES-07). |
| SB-08 | Dependencies are scanned; no known Critical or High vulnerability ships. |
| SB-09 | Source is scanned with static analysis and a secret scanner. |
| SB-10 | Web responses carry security headers (content security policy, framing, content-type options). |
| SB-11 | Deployed processes run with least privilege (e.g. non-root containers). |

## Personal data (privacy)

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-12 | Collect only the personal data a requirement needs; the project lists it. |
| SB-13 | Each personal-data item has a stated purpose and retention period. |
| SB-14 | Consent, where required, is explicit and never preselected. |
===== 00_general/skills/write-acceptance-tests/SKILL.md
---
name: write-acceptance-tests
description: Write and freeze the black-box acceptance tests from the given acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios and the contracts, before any production code exists (phase 3).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 3 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/phases.md`
- Writes: acceptance and end-to-end tests, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`
- Does not read: production source code

## Procedure

1. For every AC, write at least one test through the component's public interface that checks the observable outcome the AC states. For a rejection AC, also check that nothing changed. For every scenario in `e2e-scenarios.md`, write exactly one end-to-end test; write no other end-to-end test, and do not split or merge scenarios.
2. Put the AC id in each test name.
3. Run the suite. Every test must fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a build, configuration or harness error; a test that passes only on bootstrap code is listed in step 4. Fix the harness until that holds.
4. Record the run (pass/fail counts and a one-line reason per group of failures) in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`.
5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. Check what each helper returns and what each matcher compares (known cases: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver returns java.sql.Timestamp, not OffsetDateTime, for 	imestamptz unless the type is requested; AssertJ doesNotContain on a  yte[] tests single bytes, not a byte sequence, so compare the first bytes with Arrays.copyOf instead). A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.
===== 00_general/skills/verify-release/SKILL.md
---
name: verify-release
description: Verify the finished system with evidence: definition of done, frozen tests, security baseline and scanners, secret leaks, runtime flows, traceability, and verify → fix → re-verify loops (phase 6).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 6 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: all of `01_input/`, `docs/`, source code
- Writes: `docs/06_verification-report.md` (findings `F-nn`)

## Procedure

1. Re-read the requirements (`project/01_requirements/*`, `docs/02_*`) before checking anything.
2. Recompute every hash in `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` and `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256`. Any mismatch is a Critical finding, whatever the reason.
3. Run the full test suite and every check command (ES-05). Coverage and mutation score were recorded in phase 5; re-measure them only for a component whose code or tests changed since, once, after the last fix, as `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` defines (including \
4. Start every component as described for its target environment and exercise the core user flows at runtime; record what was run and what was observed.
5. Security: for every `SB` and `SR` item, record where it is implemented and how it was checked (test, scan, or inspection). An item without evidence is a finding.
6. Run every scanner listed under `tooling` with a security purpose (dependency, static analysis, secrets); archive raw output in `out/logs/`. Run the dependency scan **online** with the NVD key from `.env` and never with Maven's `-o` (offline) flag: offline it reuses the report of phase 0 and the suppressions do not apply, which wastes a run.
7. Classify each finding with the severity scale. For a dependency vulnerability, check whether the vulnerable feature is used. If you propose lowering a Critical or High on that basis, record the evidence and raise a blocking decision.
8. Check logs and error responses produced during testing for personal data, secrets and internals. Then check that no `.env` value leaked, listing file names only and never the values (no output means clean; any name listed is a Critical finding):
   - files: `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 grep -lF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')`
   - commit messages: `git log --all --format=%B | grep -cF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')` (must print `0`)
9. Run `node 01_input/00_general/skills/verify-release/trace-ac.mjs` once from the repository root: it prints the table AC → tests → commits (a test counts when its file names the AC or a range that contains it; a commit counts when its subject names the AC, a range that contains it, or its user story). Paste the output into the report and do not build the table by hand. An AC with no test or no commit is a finding. Commit size, message length and bursts are measured by the report afterwards, so do not audit commits here.
10. For each general and project DoD item, record evidence or a finding.
11. For every Critical or High finding, run verify → fix → re-verify and log each loop; triage Medium and Low as fixed, accepted with a reason, or open item.
12. Confirm every decision record has a resolution or is marked pending review.
13. State at the top of the report that it is a self-check, not an independent review.

- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.
===== 00_general/quality/severity-scale.md
# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |

# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.
===== 00_general/security/security-baseline.md
# Security baseline

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 0, 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project. Project requirements (`SR-nn`) and the chosen standard level are in `project/02_design/security-requirements.md`.

## Verification standard by component type

| Component type | Standard | Default level |
|---|---|---|
| Web app, API, service | OWASP ASVS (latest) | Level 1; Level 2 when handling authentication, payments or sensitive personal data |
| Mobile app | OWASP MASVS (latest) | L1 |
| Desktop app, CLI, library | Applicable OWASP ASVS chapters | Level 1 |

## Controls for every project

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | All input is validated on the trusted side (server or core), whatever the client does. |
| SB-02 | Every non-public operation checks authentication and authorization. |
| SB-03 | Credentials are stored only as salted, slow hashes; secrets come from configuration (ES-01, ES-02). |
| SB-04 | Data in transit uses TLS outside the local machine. |
| SB-05 | Output is encoded for its context; queries are parameterised. |
| SB-06 | Public and authentication endpoints are rate limited. |
| SB-07 | Errors and logs expose no internals, secrets or personal data (ES-07). |
| SB-08 | Dependencies are scanned; no known Critical or High vulnerability ships. |
| SB-09 | Source is scanned with static analysis and a secret scanner. |
| SB-10 | Web responses carry security headers (content security policy, framing, content-type options). |
| SB-11 | Deployed processes run with least privilege (e.g. non-root containers). |

## Personal data (privacy)

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-12 | Collect only the personal data a requirement needs; the project lists it. |
| SB-13 | Each personal-data item has a stated purpose and retention period. |
| SB-14 | Consent, where required, is explicit and never preselected. |

---
name: write-acceptance-tests
description: Write and freeze the black-box acceptance tests from the given acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios and the contracts, before any production code exists (phase 3).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 3 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/phases.md`
- Writes: acceptance and end-to-end tests, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`
- Does not read: production source code

## Procedure

1. For every AC, write at least one test through the component's public interface that checks the observable outcome the AC states. For a rejection AC, also check that nothing changed. For every scenario in `e2e-scenarios.md`, write exactly one end-to-end test; write no other end-to-end test, and do not split or merge scenarios.
2. Put the AC id in each test name.
3. Run the suite. Every test must fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a build, configuration or harness error; a test that passes only on bootstrap code is listed in step 4. Fix the harness until that holds.
4. Record the run (pass/fail counts and a one-line reason per group of failures) in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`.
5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. Check what each helper returns and what each matcher compares (known cases: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver returns java.sql.Timestamp, not OffsetDateTime, for 	imestamptz unless the type is requested; AssertJ doesNotContain on a  yte[] tests single bytes, not a byte sequence, so compare the first bytes with Arrays.copyOf instead). A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.

description: Verify the finished system with evidence: definition of done, frozen tests, security baseline and scanners, secret leaks, runtime flows, traceability, and verify → fix → re-verify loops (phase 6).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 6 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: all of `01_input/`, `docs/`, source code
- Writes: `docs/06_verification-report.md` (findings `F-nn`)

## Procedure

1. Re-read the requirements (`project/01_requirements/*`, `docs/02_*`) before checking anything.
2. Recompute every hash in `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` and `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256`. Any mismatch is a Critical finding, whatever the reason.
3. Run the full test suite and every check command (ES-05). Coverage and mutation score were recorded in phase 5; re-measure them only for a component whose code or tests changed since, once, after the last fix, as `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` defines (including \
4. Start every component as described for its target environment and exercise the core user flows at runtime; record what was run and what was observed.
5. Security: for every `SB` and `SR` item, record where it is implemented and how it was checked (test, scan, or inspection). An item without evidence is a finding.
6. Run every scanner listed under `tooling` with a security purpose (dependency, static analysis, secrets); archive raw output in `out/logs/`. Run the dependency scan **online** with the NVD key from `.env` and never with Maven's `-o` (offline) flag: offline it reuses the report of phase 0 and the suppressions do not apply, which wastes a run.
7. Classify each finding with the severity scale. For a dependency vulnerability, check whether the vulnerable feature is used. If you propose lowering a Critical or High on that basis, record the evidence and raise a blocking decision.
8. Check logs and error responses produced during testing for personal data, secrets and internals. Then check that no `.env` value leaked, listing file names only and never the values (no output means clean; any name listed is a Critical finding):
   - files: `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 grep -lF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')`
   - commit messages: `git log --all --format=%B | grep -cF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')` (must print `0`)
9. Run `node 01_input/00_general/skills/verify-release/trace-ac.mjs` once from the repository root: it prints the table AC → tests → commits (a test counts when its file names the AC or a range that contains it; a commit counts when its subject names the AC, a range that contains it, or its user story). Paste the output into the report and do not build the table by hand. An AC with no test or no commit is a finding. Commit size, message length and bursts are measured by the report afterwards, so do not audit commits here.
10. For each general and project DoD item, record evidence or a finding.
11. For every Critical or High finding, run verify → fix → re-verify and log each loop; triage Medium and Low as fixed, accepted with a reason, or open item.
12. Confirm every decision record has a resolution or is marked pending review.
13. State at the top of the report that it is a self-check, not an independent review.

===== user-stories.md
# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).
===== business-rules.md
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.

 Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |# Scope

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration
- Integration with an identity provider

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

## Open questions

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | Are all options available to students, or are some only for external participants? | Product owner | Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |
| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |
| OQ-05 | Is a second registration with the same email allowed? | Product owner | Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |
| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

The answers are the product owner's decisions and hold for every run of this project; the agent records no decision for them. A new question that arises later becomes a decision record as usual.
===== acceptance-criteria.md
# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |

| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).
===== business-rules.md
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)

- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |

| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
    <version>4.1.1</version>
    <relativePath/>
  </parent>

  <groupId>si.konferenca</groupId>
  <artifactId>registration-backend</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
  <name>registration-backend</name>
  <description>Conference registration REST API</description>

  <properties>
    <java.version>21</java.version>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
    <project.reporting.outputEncoding>UTF-8</project.reporting.outputEncoding>

    <!-- Overrides of Boot-managed versions (tech-stack.md) -->
    <tomcat.version>11.0.26</tomcat.version>
    <log4j2.version>2.26.1</log4j2.version>
    <commons-lang3.version>3.20.0</commons-lang3.version>
    <flyway.version>12.4.0</flyway.version>
    <postgresql.version>42.7.13</postgresql.version>
    <testcontainers.version>2.0.5</testcontainers.version>

    <!-- Versions not managed by Boot (tech-stack.md) -->
    <poi.version>5.5.1</poi.version>
    <archunit.version>1.3.2</archunit.version>

    <!-- Tooling (tech-stack.md) -->
    <spotless-maven-plugin.version>2.44.3</spotless-maven-plugin.version>
    <spotbugs-maven-plugin.version>4.10.4.1</spotbugs-maven-plugin.version>
    <maven-pmd-plugin.version>3.26.0</maven-pmd-plugin.version>
    <jacoco-maven-plugin.version>0.8.12</jacoco-maven-plugin.version>
    <pitest-maven.version>1.30.0</pitest-maven.version>
    <pitest-junit5-plugin.version>1.2.3</pitest-junit5-plugin.version>
    <dependency-check-maven.version>12.1.0</dependency-check-maven.version>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-webmvc</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-mail</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-flyway</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-database-postgresql</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
      <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.poi</groupId>
      <artifactId>poi-ooxml</artifactId>
      <version>${poi.version}</version>
    </dependency>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
      <artifactId>testcontainers-junit-jupiter</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
      <artifactId>testcontainers-postgresql</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.tngtech.archunit</groupId>
      <artifactId>archunit-junit5</artifactId>
      <version>${archunit.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
          <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>${jacoco-maven-plugin.version}</version>
        </plugin>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
          <artifactId>pitest-maven</artifactId>
          <version>${pitest-maven.version}</version>
          <dependencies>
            <dependency>
              <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
              <artifactId>pitest-junit5-plugin</artifactId>
              <version>${pitest-junit5-plugin.version}</version>
            </dependency>
          </dependencies>
        </plugin>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.owasp</groupId>
          <artifactId>dependency-check-maven</artifactId>
          <version>${dependency-check-maven.version}</version>
          <configuration>
            <nvdApiKeyEnvironmentVariable>NVD_API_KEY</nvdApiKeyEnvironmentVariable>
            <failBuildOnCVSS>7</failBuildOnCVSS>
            <formats>
              <format>HTML</format>
              <format>JSON</format>
            </formats>
          </configuration>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>

    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>com.diffplug.spotless</groupId>
        <artifactId>spotless-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${spotless-maven-plugin.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <java>
            <googleJavaFormat/>
            <removeUnusedImports/>
          </java>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-pmd-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${maven-pmd-plugin.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <rulesets>
            <ruleset>/rulesets/java/quickstart.xml</ruleset>
          </rulesets>
          <printFailingErrors>true</printFailingErrors>
          <linkXRef>false</linkXRef>
          <minimumTokens>100</minimumTokens>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>com.github.spotbugs</groupId>
        <artifactId>spotbugs-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${spotbugs-maven-plugin.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <effort>Max</effort>
          <threshold>Medium</threshold>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

> Written in: phase 0 · Source: `project/00_setup/*` · Procedure: `general/skills/preflight` · Agent: writes

| Check | Source of truth | Result |

| Run configuration complete | `project/00_setup/run-config.md` | |
| Platforms and tools installed at the listed versions | `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` | |

| Every listed dependency resolves | `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` | |
| No listed dependency has a known Critical or High vulnerability | `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` | |
| Clean working tree on the starting commit | repository | |
| Input manifest written | `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256` | |

## Dependency results

| id | version | Resolves | Highest vulnerability |
|---|---|---|---|

## Asked the human

| When | What was missing | Answer | Re-check |
|---|---|---|---|
# Decisions log

> Written in: every phase · Format: `general/working-rules.md` ("Decision record") · Agent: appends only
# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started automatically by the Stop and SessionEnd hooks in `.claude/settings.json` once `run-log.json` has an `end`; if the hooks did not run, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Nothing is typed in by hand. The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-summary.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

input.content:
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Conference registration API
  version: 0.1.0
  description: |
    REST API of the registration backend (AR-01). All paths are under `/api`.
    Every `/api` endpoint is rate limited per client IP (SR-03) and request bodies
    are limited to `REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (default 16384) bytes. Error bodies never
    contain stack traces, class names, SQL or configuration values (SB-07).
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary
servers:
  - url: /
tags:
  - name: registration
  - name: organizer
security: []
paths:
  /api/form-config:
    get:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: getFormConfig
      summary: Form configuration (active options, consents, anti-automation mode)
      description: |
        Lists only active options (AC-003-01), in configuration order, each with the
        registration types it is available to (OQ-01), and every configured consent (OQ-02).
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Form configuration
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/FormConfig'
        '429':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/TooManyRequests'
  /api/registrations:
    post:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: createRegistration
      summary: Submit a registration
      description: |
        Validates the submission (BR-01 … BR-05, SR-04), verifies the reCAPTCHA token
        on the backend (SR-01), stores the database row and the JSON copy in one
        transaction (BR-07, AR-05), answers 201, then sends the participant and
        organizer emails (OQ-03: a mail failure does not change the answer).
        Field validation runs first; the token is verified only when every field is
        valid. Any rejection stores nothing and sends no email.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/RegistrationRequest'
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Registration accepted and stored
          headers:
            Location:
              description: /api/registrations/{id} (informational; there is no public read endpoint)
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/RegistrationAccepted'
        '400':
          description: Rejected; nothing stored, no email sent
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationError'
        '413':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge'
        '415':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/GeneralError'
        '429':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/TooManyRequests'
        '500':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/GeneralError'
  /api/registrations/export:
    get:
      tags: [organizer]
      operationId: exportRegistrations
      summary: Excel export of every stored registration (organizer only)

# Email contract (SMTP)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03 · Agent: writes

Both emails are sent after the database transaction (with the JSON copy) has committed, after the 201 answer has been decided, by the backend through the configured SMTP server (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, optional `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`). Connection and read timeouts are 5 s. A failure of either email is logged as `Email <kind> for registration <id> failed` with no personal data and does not change the API answer (OQ-03).

## Common rules (SR-05)

- `From`: `MAIL_FROM` (setting, default `registration@konferenca.local`).
- Content: `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` only, no HTML part. User input appears only in the body, so markup is literal text.
- Headers never contain user input: the subject is built from `CONFERENCE_NAME` only; recipients are addresses that passed the email rule (no whitespace, so no CR/LF) or configured organizer addresses; no display names.
- Exactly one recipient per message in `To`; no `Cc` or `Bcc`.

## Participant confirmation (US-006, AC-006-01, AC-006-02)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email (trimmed) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmation – <CONFERENCE_NAME>` |
| Body | lines, in order: `Dear <firstName> <lastName>,` · blank · `your registration for <CONFERENCE_NAME> has been received.` · blank · `Registration ID: <id>` · `Registration type: External participant` or `Student` · blank · `Selected options:` · one line `- <option name> (<Workshop|Event|Meal|Other activity>)` per selected option, or `- none` · blank · `Kind regards,` · `<CONFERENCE_NAME> organizers` |

## Organizer notification (US-007, AC-007-01, AC-007-02, SR-07)

One message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, each trimmed and validated at start-up; an invalid address stops start-up).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | one organizer address |
| Subject | `New registration – <CONFERENCE_NAME>` |
| Body | `A new registration was received.` · blank · then one `Label: value` line each for `Registration ID`, `Registration type`, `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC), `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, and either `Organization / institution` or `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID` · blank · `Selected options:` with lines as in the participant email · blank · `Consents:` with one line `- <consent id>: given at <ISO-8601 UTC>` per consent |
| Attachment | `registration-<id>.json`, content type `application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`) |

Only registration data appears (SR-07): no internal ids other than the registration id, no configuration values, no server information.
