# UI contract (registration page)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-001, US-002, US-004, BR-01, BR-04 … BR-06, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07 · Agent: writes

The frontend's public interface for acceptance (component) tests and end-to-end tests. Texts and accessible names below are exact (case-sensitive); tests select elements by role, label and the `data-testid` values listed here, never by CSS class or internal structure.

## Module and network

- `src/App.tsx` exports a named React component `App` with no props; `src/main.tsx` only mounts it.
- The app calls the global `fetch` with relative string URLs only (AR-01):
  - on mount: `fetch("/api/form-config")` → `FormConfig` (`openapi.yaml`);
  - on submit: `fetch("/api/registrations", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(RegistrationRequest) })`.
- The request body contains `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, the type's own fields only, `optionIds` (selected ids in configuration order), `consents` (every configured consent id → checkbox state) and `recaptchaToken`.
- No secret is bundled (AR-07); the reCAPTCHA site key comes from `FormConfig.captcha.siteKey`.

## States

| State | What is shown |
|---|---|
| Loading | text `Loading…` |
| Configuration failed (non-200 or network error) | an element with role `alert` and text `The registration form is currently unavailable. Please try again later.`; no form |
| Ready, no type chosen | heading level 1 `Conference registration`; the conference name as a paragraph; the type choice; no field, option, consent or submit button |
| Ready, type chosen | the type choice, the type's fields, options, consents, anti-automation control, button `Register` |
| Submitting | button `Register` disabled |
| Accepted (201) | heading level 2 `Registration received`; text `Thank you, <firstName> <lastName>.` (values from the response); a list (role `list`, accessible name `Selected options`) with one item per selected option name, or the text `No options selected.`; no form, no `Register` button |
| Rejected (400) | the form with every entered value kept, and each field error next to its field (below) |
| Other failure (any other status, network error, invalid response) | the form with values kept and an element with role `alert`, text `Registration could not be completed. Please try again later.`; no technical detail |

## Type choice

A `radiogroup` (fieldset) with legend `Registration type` and two radios, none checked initially: `External participant` (value `EXTERNAL`), `Student` (value `STUDENT`). Switching type keeps the shared fields' values.

## Fields (labels are the accessible names)

| API field | Label | Shown for |
|---|---|---|
| firstName | `First name` | both |
| lastName | `Last name` | both |
| email | `Email` (input type `email`, `noValidate` on the form) | both |
| organization | `Organization / institution` | EXTERNAL |
| studyInstitution | `Study institution` | STUDENT |
| studyProgramme | `Study programme` | STUDENT |
| studentId | `Student ID` | STUDENT |

No other text input exists.

## Options

One `group` (fieldset) per category that has at least one active option available to the chosen type, in this order and with these legends: `Workshops` (WORKSHOP), `Events` (EVENT), `Meals` (MEAL), `Other activities` (OTHER). Each option is a checkbox whose label is the option's `name`, unchecked initially, in configuration order. Options not available to the chosen type are not rendered (OQ-01). The options group container has `data-testid="options"`.

## Consents

A `group` (fieldset) with legend `Consents`; one checkbox per configured consent, labelled with its `text`, never preselected (BR-05).

## Anti-automation

- `captcha.mode = "test"`: a checkbox labelled `I am not a robot (test mode)`; checked → token `test-pass`, unchecked → no token.
- `captcha.mode = "recaptcha"`: the Google reCAPTCHA v2 widget rendered explicitly into `<div data-testid="recaptcha">` with the site key; the token is the widget's response; after a rejected submission the widget is reset.

## Field errors (NFR-03)

Each error is rendered directly after its field or group as an element with `data-testid="error-<field>"`, and the input (or the group's fieldset) gets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at it. `<field>` is the API field name: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `options`, `consents.<consentId>`, `recaptchaToken`. Backend errors for `type` or `body` are shown in the general `alert` with the text of the "other failure" state.

Client-side validation runs on submit before any request (AC-004-03); if any rule fails, no request is sent:

| Rule | Message |
|---|---|
| required field empty or only whitespace | `This field is required.` |
| email does not match `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` after trimming | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| mandatory consent unchecked | `This consent is required.` |
| no anti-automation token | `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` |

Backend field errors (400) are shown with the backend's message text, replacing client errors for the same field. Errors are cleared on the next submit.

## Type choice

A `radiogroup` (fieldset) with legend `Registration type` and two radios, none checked initially: `External participant` (value `EXTERNAL`), `Student` (value `STUDENT`). Switching type keeps the shared fields' values.

## Fields (labels are the accessible names)

| API field | Label | Shown for |
|---|---|---|
| firstName | `First name` | both |
| lastName | `Last name` | both |
| email | `Email` (input type `email`, `noValidate` on the form) | both |
| organization | `Organization / institution` | EXTERNAL |
| studyInstitution | `Study institution` | STUDENT |
| studyProgramme | `Study programme` | STUDENT |
| studentId | `Student ID` | STUDENT |

No other text input exists.

## Options

One `group` (fieldset) per category that has at least one active option available to the chosen type, in this order and with these legends: `Workshops` (WORKSHOP), `Events` (EVENT), `Meals` (MEAL), `Other activities` (OTHER). Each option is a checkbox whose label is the option's `name`, unchecked initially, in configuration order. Options not available to the chosen type are not rendered (OQ-01). The options group container has `data-testid="options"`.

## Consents

A `group` (fieldset) with legend `Consents`; one checkbox per configured consent, labelled with its `text`, never preselected (BR-05).

## Anti-automation

- `captcha.mode = "test"`: a checkbox labelled `I am not a robot (test mode)`; checked → token `test-pass`, unchecked → no token.
- `captcha.mode = "recaptcha"`: the Google reCAPTCHA v2 widget rendered explicitly into `<div data-testid="recaptcha">` with the site key; the token is the widget's response; after a rejected submission the widget is reset.

## Field errors (NFR-03)

Each error is rendered directly after its field or group as an element with `data-testid="error-<field>"`, and the input (or the group's fieldset) gets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at it. `<field>` is the API field name: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `options`, `consents.<consentId>`, `recaptchaToken`. Backend errors for `type` or `body` are shown in the general `alert` with the text of the "other failure" state.

Client-side validation runs on submit before any request (AC-004-03); if any rule fails, no request is sent:

| Rule | Message |
|---|---|
| required field empty or only whitespace | `This field is required.` |
| email does not match `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` after trimming | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| mandatory consent unchecked | `This consent is required.` |
| no anti-automation token | `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` |

Backend field errors (400) are shown with the backend's message text, replacing client errors for the same field. Errors are cleared on the next submit.

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts (normative, `docs/02_contracts/`): `openapi.yaml` (REST), `registration-copy.schema.json` (JSON copy and attachment), `conference-config.schema.json` with the shipped instance `conference.json` (options and consents), `database.sql` (PostgreSQL schema), `emails.md` (SMTP), `ui-contract.md` (registration page). Section numbers below (§n) are referenced from the traceability table.

## §1 Components and runtime topology

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Port inside | Local exposure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot jar in `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, user `app` (uid 10001) | 8080 | none (reached through the frontend's `/api` proxy) |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | static build served by `nginx` (multi-stage: `node` build stage), user `nginx` (uid 101) | 8080 | `127.0.0.1:8080` |
| postgres | image | PostgreSQL 16, database and user `registration`, password `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | 5432 | none |
| mailpit | image | SMTP 1025, HTTP API/UI 8025 | 1025, 8025 | `127.0.0.1:8025` (API and UI) |

`02_output/docker-compose.yml` (project name `registration`) starts the four services with `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build` from `02_output/`; the backend jar is built first with `./mvnw -B package -DskipTests` (the image copies `target/*.jar`; no JDK image is in `tech-stack.md`). Named volumes: `pgdata` (database) and `jsoncopies` (mounted at `/data/json-copies` in the backend) survive `docker compose down` and `up` (NFR-02). The shipped `backend/config/conference.json` (identical to `docs/02_contracts/conference.json`) is mounted read-only at `/config/conference.json`. Health checks: backend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness`, postgres `pg_isready`, frontend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/`; the backend starts after postgres is healthy, the frontend after the backend is healthy (NFR-04, ES-09).

Production (`environments.md`): the same two images behind the external nginx, which terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend and forwards `/api` to the backend, setting `Host` to the upstream itself and `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr`, `X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme` (SR-08). The frontend container's own nginx also proxies `/api` to `http://backend:8080` with the same header rules, so the local stack behaves like production.

## §2 Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports-and-adapters, root package `si.konferenca.registration`. Declared layers:

| Package | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model, option catalogue, consent definitions, validation rules, value types; pure Java | Java SE only |
| `application` | use cases (`RegisterParticipant`, `GetFormConfiguration`, `ExportRegistrations`) and the ports they need (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring stereotype and transaction annotations |
| `adapter.web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, servlet filters (rate limit, body size, organizer HTTPS-only) | `application`, `domain`, `config` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` implementation | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.file` | `JsonCopyStore` implementation (atomic file write) | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | `RegistrationNotifier` implementation (Spring Mail) | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | `CaptchaVerifier` implementations (Google siteverify, test mode) | `application`, `domain`, `config` |
| `adapter.export` | `WorkbookWriter` implementation (Apache POI) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | `@ConfigurationProperties`, conference configuration loader, security configuration, production safety check | `application`, `domain` |
| root | `RegistrationApplication` (entry point only) | everything |

Reason: the domain rules (BR-01 … BR-05, SR-04) and the storage order (AR-05) are the risky parts; isolating them from Spring MVC, JPA, SMTP and POI makes them testable without containers and keeps each external system replaceable (production vs. test reCAPTCHA).

ArchUnit rules (`architecture` test level, phase 5; each rule names this section): (A1) `domain` depends on no other project package and on no `org.springframework`, `jakarta.persistence`, `org.apache.poi` class; (A2) `application` depends only on `domain` among project packages; (A3) no `adapter.*` package depends on another `adapter.*` package, except `adapter.web` on none of them either; (A4) only `adapter.persistence` uses `jakarta.persistence` and Spring Data; only `adapter.export` uses `org.apache.poi`; only `adapter.mail` uses `org.springframework.mail`/`jakarta.mail`; (A5) slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` are free of cycles (AR-03).

## §3 Configuration (ES-01, AR-04, SR-02)

Settings come from environment variables (Spring relaxed binding); secrets have no default. "Required" settings have no default in `application.yml`: the backend does not start without them.

| Variable | Property | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USERNAME` | `spring.datasource.url`, `.username` | none (required) | local compose sets them |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `spring.datasource.password` | none (secret) | |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` | `spring.mail.host`, `.port` | none (required) | Mailpit locally |
| `SMTP_STARTTLS` | `spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.starttls.enable` (+ `.required`) | `true` | `false` only for Mailpit |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `spring.mail.username`, `.password` | empty | secrets; production only |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `app.mail.from` | `registration@konferenca.local` | |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | `app.mail.organizer-recipients` | none (required, ≥ 1 valid address) | secret-listed |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `app.conference.name` | `Conference` | shown in emails and the form |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | `app.conference.config-location` | none (required) | Spring resource location, e.g. `file:/config/conference.json` |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `app.storage.json-copy-dir` | `/data/json-copies` | created on first write if missing |
| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `app.recaptcha.test-mode` | `false` | `true` only in test and local |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | `app.recaptcha.site-key`, `.secret-key` | empty | secrets |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `app.recaptcha.verify-url` | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` | tests point it at a stub (DoD-P05) |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | `app.organizer.username`, `.password` | none (required; password ≥ 16 chars) | password kept only as a BCrypt hash after start-up |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `app.organizer.https-only` | `true` | `false` only on local plain HTTP |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `app.cors.allowed-origins` | empty (no CORS) | local Vite dev server only |
| `RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.form-config-per-minute` | `60` | per client IP |
| `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATIONS_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.registrations-per-minute` | `10` | per client IP |
| `RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.export-per-minute` | `10` | per client IP, failed logins included |
| `REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `app.request.max-body-bytes` | `16384` | |
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | | none | `prod` in production |

**Production safety check (SR-02):** with profile `prod`, start-up fails when `app.recaptcha.test-mode` is true, when either reCAPTCHA key is blank, or when `app.organizer.https-only` is false.

**Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003):** a JSON file matching `conference-config.schema.json`, read once at start-up from `CONFERENCE_CONFIG`. The loader rejects (start-up fails with a message naming the problem, AC-003-03): unreadable file, invalid JSON, unknown property, missing or blank `name` or consent `text`, unknown `category` or registration type, id not matching the pattern, duplicate option id, duplicate consent id, empty `availableTo`. `active` defaults to `true`, `availableTo` to both types. Changing options means editing this file and restarting; the participant fields are code and never configurable (BR-01). The shipped file has active options in all four categories for external participants, options available to one type only, and one inactive option (`docs/02_contracts/conference.json`).

## §4 Registration use case (US-001, US-002, US-004 … US-007)

1. **Parse** (`adapter.web`): JSON body ≤ `REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (else 413), `Content-Type: application/json` (else 415). Malformed JSON or an unknown property → 400 with field `body`.
2. **Normalise:** every text value is trimmed (BR-02); `null` option list → empty; `null` consents → empty.
3. **Validate** (`domain`, all errors collected, SB-01), messages exact:

| Field | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| type | present, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` | `Choose a registration type.` (then no type-specific checks) |
| firstName, lastName, email, organization (EXTERNAL), studyInstitution, studyProgramme, studentId (STUDENT) | non-blank after trimming | `This field is required.` |
| same | length ≤ 100 (names), 254 (email), 200 (organization, study institution, study programme), 50 (student ID) | `Must be at most <n> characters.` |
| email | matches `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| fields of the other type | absent, null or blank | `Not allowed for this registration type.` |
| options | ≤ 50 ids; each id known, active and available to the type (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01); no id twice (OQ-04) | `Option '<id>' is not available.` / `Option '<id>' is selected more than once.` / `Too many options.` (field `options`, one error per problem) |
| consents.<id> | every mandatory consent present with `true` (BR-05) | `This consent is required.` |
| consents.<id> | id is a configured consent | `Unknown consent.` |
| recaptchaToken | non-blank | `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` |

Text otherwise accepts any Unicode, including line breaks and markup (AC-006-02); it is never interpreted.
4. **Verify the token** (only if step 3 found no error; SR-01): `CaptchaVerifier`. Production: `POST RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` form-encoded `secret`, `response` (and `remoteip`), timeout 5 s; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. Any other answer, non-200 status or I/O error → rejected. Test mode: accepted only for the token `test-pass`. Rejected → 400, field `recaptchaToken`, `Anti-automation check failed. Please try again.`
5. **Store** (`application`, one database transaction, AR-05, BR-07): generate a random UUID and `registeredAt` (UTC, truncated to milliseconds; consents `givenAt` = `registeredAt`); insert the rows (`database.sql`); serialise the JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`, field order as in the schema, UTF-8) and write it to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json` via a temporary file and an atomic move; then commit. If the JSON write fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 `Registration could not be stored. Please try again later.` (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the file was written, the file is deleted.
6. **Answer** 201 with `RegistrationAccepted` and `Location`.
7. **Notify** after commit (OQ-03, `emails.md`): participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per address with the stored JSON bytes attached. Exceptions are caught and logged with the registration id only (ES-07).

Second registrations with the same email are stored separately (OQ-05). Retention: no automatic deletion (OQ-06); the release notes carry the 12-month deletion instruction.

## §5 Form configuration (US-003)

`GET /api/form-config` returns `conferenceName`, the active options in configuration order with `availableTo` (AC-003-01), the consents, and `captcha` = `{mode: "test", siteKey: null}` in test mode or `{mode: "recaptcha", siteKey}` otherwise (AR-07). The response is computed from the configuration loaded at start-up, so a restart with another file changes it with no code change (AC-003-02).

## §6 Export (US-008)

`GET /api/registrations/export`, organizer only (BR-08, SB-02):

- Filter order: rate limit → organizer HTTPS-only check → Basic authentication → controller. HTTPS-only: when `app.organizer.https-only` is true and the request is not secure (after `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted proxy) and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 `{"message":"Organizer access requires HTTPS."}` (SR-06, D-10).
- Authentication: Spring Security HTTP Basic, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` with the BCrypt hash of `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (SB-03), role `ORGANIZER`. Missing or wrong credentials → 401 `{"message":"Authentication required."}` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`, no data (AC-008-02).
- Workbook (`.xlsx`, POI `XSSFWorkbook`), sheet `Registrations`, header row then one row per registration ordered by `registeredAt` (AC-008-01). Columns: `Registration ID`, `Type` (`EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT`), `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC), `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities` (selected option names of that category joined by `; `), `Consents` (`<id> (<givenAt>)` joined by `; `). Every cell is a string cell, so text is unchanged (NFR-01, AC-008-03) and never evaluated as a formula. Only registration data (SR-07).
- Headers: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## §7 Web security (SB, SR)

- Spring Security: stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies or sessions are used; the only authenticated call is a read with Basic credentials). Permit `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness`; export as §6; everything else denied (403). Actuator exposes `health` only, without details.
- Headers on every backend response (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Frontend nginx headers (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; `client_max_body_size 16k`; `server_tokens off`; `proxy_set_header Host $proxy_host` (SR-08).
- Rate limit (SR-03, SB-06): servlet filter before Spring Security, fixed one-minute window per (client IP, group) with the limits of §3; over the limit → 429 `{"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}` with `Retry-After`. Client IP is `request.getRemoteAddr()` after Tomcat's `RemoteIpValve` (`server.forward-headers-strategy: native`, trusting only private and loopback proxy addresses).
- Body size (SR-03): filter rejects a declared or actual body above the limit with 413 `{"message":"Request too large."}`.
- Errors (SB-07, ES-07): one `@RestControllerAdvice`; unexpected exceptions → 500 `{"message":"An unexpected error occurred."}`; `server.error.include-*` never; logs carry registration ids, never names, emails, tokens or credentials.
- CORS: only the origins in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, methods GET/POST, no credentials.
- SQL only through JPA with bound parameters (SB-05).

## §8 Frontend (US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03)

React single page as defined in `ui-contract.md`: modules `api` (fetch calls and response parsing), `validation` (client rules mirroring §4 required/email/consent/token rules), `RegistrationForm`, `OptionGroups`, `Consents`, `Captcha` (test checkbox or Google widget loaded with `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js?render=explicit`), `Confirmation`. All server text is rendered as React text (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, SB-05). Only relative `/api` URLs (AR-01).

## §9 Test levels and harness

| Level | Component | Location | Harness |
|---|---|---|---|
| acceptance | backend | `backend/src/test/java/si/konferenca/registration/acceptance/` | `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` over real HTTP (`java.net.http.HttpClient`), PostgreSQL and Mailpit through Testcontainers (`postgres:16.15-alpine`, `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1`, Mailpit API for received mail), reCAPTCHA test mode, test configuration files under `src/test/resources/acceptance/`; database checked with `JdbcTemplate`, JSON copies on a temporary directory |
| acceptance | frontend | `frontend/tests/acceptance/` | Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom, `App` rendered, global `fetch` stubbed per `openapi.yaml` |
| e2e | all | `frontend/e2e/` (`playwright.config.ts`, `testDir: e2e`) | Playwright Chromium against `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (local stack, `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`); database via `docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U registration -d registration`, JSON copies via `docker compose exec -T backend ls/cat /data/json-copies`, mail via Mailpit API `http://127.0.0.1:8025/api/v1/`, export via Playwright `request` with `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`/`ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from the environment |
| unit, integration, architecture | each | other test paths | phase 5 |

The local stack for e2e runs with `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`, `SMTP_STARTTLS=false`, `CONFERENCE_NAME=Konferenca 2026` and `CONFERENCE_CONFIG=file:/config/conference.json`.

## §10 Non-functional requirements

| NFR | Design |
|---|---|
| NFR-01 | UTF-8 end to end: PostgreSQL `UTF8`, JSON copy UTF-8 without escaping non-ASCII, `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` mail, xlsx string cells, `lang` and `<meta charset="UTF-8">` in the page |
| NFR-02 | named volumes `pgdata`, `jsoncopies` (§1); demonstrated in phase 6 with `docker compose down` / `up` |
| NFR-03 | `ui-contract.md` client rules and backend error placement |
| NFR-04 | actuator liveness and readiness (database included) and compose health checks (§1) |

## §4 Registration use case (US-001, US-002, US-004 … US-007)

1. **Parse** (`adapter.web`): JSON body ≤ `REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (else 413), `Content-Type: application/json` (else 415). Malformed JSON or an unknown property → 400 with field `body`.
2. **Normalise:** every text value is trimmed (BR-02); `null` option list → empty; `null` consents → empty.
3. **Validate** (`domain`, all errors collected, SB-01), messages exact:

| Field | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| type | present, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` | `Choose a registration type.` (then no type-specific checks) |
| firstName, lastName, email, organization (EXTERNAL), studyInstitution, studyProgramme, studentId (STUDENT) | non-blank after trimming | `This field is required.` |
| same | length ≤ 100 (names), 254 (email), 200 (organization, study institution, study programme), 50 (student ID) | `Must be at most <n> characters.` |
| email | matches `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| fields of the other type | absent, null or blank | `Not allowed for this registration type.` |
| options | ≤ 50 ids; each id known, active and available to the type (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01); no id twice (OQ-04) | `Option '<id>' is not available.` / `Option '<id>' is selected more than once.` / `Too many options.` (field `options`, one error per problem) |
| consents.<id> | every mandatory consent present with `true` (BR-05) | `This consent is required.` |
| consents.<id> | id is a configured consent | `Unknown consent.` |
| recaptchaToken | non-blank | `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` |

Text otherwise accepts any Unicode, including line breaks and markup (AC-006-02); it is never interpreted.
4. **Verify the token** (only if step 3 found no error; SR-01): `CaptchaVerifier`. Production: `POST RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` form-encoded `secret`, `response` (and `remoteip`), timeout 5 s; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. Any other answer, non-200 status or I/O error → rejected. Test mode: accepted only for the token `test-pass`. Rejected → 400, field `recaptchaToken`, `Anti-automation check failed. Please try again.`
5. **Store** (`application`, one database transaction, AR-05, BR-07): generate a random UUID and `registeredAt` (UTC, truncated to milliseconds; consents `givenAt` = `registeredAt`); insert the rows (`database.sql`); serialise the JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`, field order as in the schema, UTF-8) and write it to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json` via a temporary file and an atomic move; then commit. If the JSON write fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 `Registration could not be stored. Please try again later.` (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the file was written, the file is deleted.
6. **Answer** 201 with `RegistrationAccepted` and `Location`.
7. **Notify** after commit (OQ-03, `emails.md`): participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per address with the stored JSON bytes attached. Exceptions are caught and logged with the registration id only (ES-07).

Second registrations with the same email are stored separately (OQ-05). Retention: no automatic deletion (OQ-06); the release notes carry the 12-month deletion instruction.

## §5 Form configuration (US-003)

`GET /api/form-config` returns `conferenceName`, the active options in configuration order with `availableTo` (AC-003-01), the consents, and `captcha` = `{mode: "test", siteKey: null}` in test mode or `{mode: "recaptcha", siteKey}` otherwise (AR-07). The response is computed from the configuration loaded at start-up, so a restart with another file changes it with no code change (AC-003-02).

## §6 Export (US-008)

`GET /api/registrations/export`, organizer only (BR-08, SB-02):

- Filter order: rate limit → organizer HTTPS-only check → Basic authentication → controller. HTTPS-only: when `app.organizer.https-only` is true and the request is not secure (after `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted proxy) and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 `{"message":"Organizer access requires HTTPS."}` (SR-06, D-10).
- Authentication: Spring Security HTTP Basic, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` with the BCrypt hash of `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (SB-03), role `ORGANIZER`. Missing or wrong credentials → 401 `{"message":"Authentication required."}` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`, no data (AC-008-02).
- Workbook (`.xlsx`, POI `XSSFWorkbook`), sheet `Registrations`, header row then one row per registration ordered by `registeredAt` (AC-008-01). Columns: `Registration ID`, `Type` (`EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT`), `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC), `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities` (selected option names of that category joined by `; `), `Consents` (`<id> (<givenAt>)` joined by `; `). Every cell is a string cell, so text is unchanged (NFR-01, AC-008-03) and never evaluated as a formula. Only registration data (SR-07).
- Headers: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## §7 Web security (SB, SR)

- Spring Security: stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies or sessions are used; the only authenticated call is a read with Basic credentials). Permit `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness`; export as §6; everything else denied (403). Actuator exposes `health` only, without details.
- Headers on every backend response (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Frontend nginx headers (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; `client_max_body_size 16k`; `server_tokens off`; `proxy_set_header Host $proxy_host` (SR-08).
- Rate limit (SR-03, SB-06): servlet filter before Spring Security, fixed one-minute window per (client IP, group) with the limits of §3; over the limit → 429 `{"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}` with `Retry-After`. Client IP is `request.getRemoteAddr()` after Tomcat's `RemoteIpValve` (`server.forward-headers-strategy: native`, trusting only private and loopback proxy addresses).
- Body size (SR-03): filter rejects a declared or actual body above the limit with 413 `{"message":"Request too large."}`.
- Errors (SB-07, ES-07): one `@RestControllerAdvice`; unexpected exceptions → 500 `{"message":"An unexpected error occurred."}`; `server.error.include-*` never; logs carry registration ids, never names, emails, tokens or credentials.
- CORS: only the origins in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, methods GET/POST, no credentials.
- SQL only through JPA with bound parameters (SB-05).

## §8 Frontend (US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03)

React single page as defined in `ui-contract.md`: modules `api` (fetch calls and response parsing), `validation` (client rules mirroring §4 required/email/consent/token rules), `RegistrationForm`, `OptionGroups`, `Consents`, `Captcha` (test checkbox or Google widget loaded with `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js?render=explicit`), `Confirmation`. All server text is rendered as React text (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, SB-05). Only relative `/api` URLs (AR-01).

| Level | Component | Location | Harness |
|---|---|---|---|
| acceptance | backend | `backend/src/test/java/si/konferenca/registration/acceptance/` | `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` over real HTTP (`java.net.http.HttpClient`), PostgreSQL and Mailpit through Testcontainers (`postgres:16.15-alpine`, `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1`, Mailpit API for received mail), reCAPTCHA test mode, test configuration files under `src/test/resources/acceptance/`; database checked with `JdbcTemplate`, JSON copies on a temporary directory |

## §4 Registration use case (US-001, US-002, US-004 … US-007)

1. **Parse** (`adapter.web`): JSON body ≤ `REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (else 413), `Content-Type: application/json` (else 415). Malformed JSON or an unknown property → 400 with field `body`.
2. **Normalise:** every text value is trimmed (BR-02); `null` option list → empty; `null` consents → empty.
3. **Validate** (`domain`, all errors collected, SB-01), messages exact:

| Field | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| type | present, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` | `Choose a registration type.` (then no type-specific checks) |
| firstName, lastName, email, organization (EXTERNAL), studyInstitution, studyProgramme, studentId (STUDENT) | non-blank after trimming | `This field is required.` |
| same | length ≤ 100 (names), 254 (email), 200 (organization, study institution, study programme), 50 (student ID) | `Must be at most <n> characters.` |
| email | matches `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| fields of the other type | absent, null or blank | `Not allowed for this registration type.` |
| options | ≤ 50 ids; each id known, active and available to the type (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01); no id twice (OQ-04) | `Option '<id>' is not available.` / `Option '<id>' is selected more than once.` / `Too many options.` (field `options`, one error per problem) |
| consents.<id> | every mandatory consent present with `true` (BR-05) | `This consent is required.` |
| consents.<id> | id is a configured consent | `Unknown consent.` |
| recaptchaToken | non-blank | `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` |

Text otherwise accepts any Unicode, including line breaks and markup (AC-006-02); it is never interpreted.
4. **Verify the token** (only if step 3 found no error; SR-01): `CaptchaVerifier`. Production: `POST RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` form-encoded `secret`, `response` (and `remoteip`), timeout 5 s; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. Any other answer, non-200 status or I/O error → rejected. Test mode: accepted only for the token `test-pass`. Rejected → 400, field `recaptchaToken`, `Anti-automation check failed. Please try again.`
5. **Store** (`application`, one database transaction, AR-05, BR-07): generate a random UUID and `registeredAt` (UTC, truncated to milliseconds; consents `givenAt` = `registeredAt`); insert the rows (`database.sql`); serialise the JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`, field order as in the schema, UTF-8) and write it to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json` via a temporary file and an atomic move; then commit. If the JSON write fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 `Registration could not be stored. Please try again later.` (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the file was written, the file is deleted.
6. **Answer** 201 with `RegistrationAccepted` and `Location`.
7. **Notify** after commit (OQ-03, `emails.md`): participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per address with the stored JSON bytes attached. Exceptions are caught and logged with the registration id only (ES-07).

Second registrations with the same email are stored separately (OQ-05). Retention: no automatic deletion (OQ-06); the release notes carry the 12-month deletion instruction.

## §5 Form configuration (US-003)

`GET /api/form-config` returns `conferenceName`, the active options in configuration order with `availableTo` (AC-003-01), the consents, and `captcha` = `{mode: "test", siteKey: null}` in test mode or `{mode: "recaptcha", siteKey}` otherwise (AR-07). The response is computed from the configuration loaded at start-up, so a restart with another file changes it with no code change (AC-003-02).

## §6 Export (US-008)

`GET /api/registrations/export`, organizer only (BR-08, SB-02):

- Filter order: rate limit → organizer HTTPS-only check → Basic authentication → controller. HTTPS-only: when `app.organizer.https-only` is true and the request is not secure (after `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted proxy) and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 `{"message":"Organizer access requires HTTPS."}` (SR-06, D-10).
- Authentication: Spring Security HTTP Basic, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` with the BCrypt hash of `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (SB-03), role `ORGANIZER`. Missing or wrong credentials → 401 `{"message":"Authentication required."}` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`, no data (AC-008-02).
- Workbook (`.xlsx`, POI `XSSFWorkbook`), sheet `Registrations`, header row then one row per registration ordered by `registeredAt` (AC-008-01). Columns: `Registration ID`, `Type` (`EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT`), `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC), `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities` (selected option names of that category joined by `; `), `Consents` (`<id> (<givenAt>)` joined by `; `). Every cell is a string cell, so text is unchanged (NFR-01, AC-008-03) and never evaluated as a formula. Only registration data (SR-07).
- Headers: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## §7 Web security (SB, SR)

- Spring Security: stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies or sessions are used; the only authenticated call is a read with Basic credentials). Permit `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness`; export as §6; everything else denied (403). Actuator exposes `health` only, without details.
- Headers on every backend response (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Frontend nginx headers (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; `client_max_body_size 16k`; `server_tokens off`; `proxy_set_header Host $proxy_host` (SR-08).
- Rate limit (SR-03, SB-06): servlet filter before Spring Security, fixed one-minute window per (client IP, group) with the limits of §3; over the limit → 429 `{"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}` with `Retry-After`. Client IP is `request.getRemoteAddr()` after Tomcat's `RemoteIpValve` (`server.forward-headers-strategy: native`, trusting only private and loopback proxy addresses).
- Body size (SR-03): filter rejects a declared or actual body above the limit with 413 `{"message":"Request too large."}`.
- Errors (SB-07, ES-07): one `@RestControllerAdvice`; unexpected exceptions → 500 `{"message":"An unexpected error occurred."}`; `server.error.include-*` never; logs carry registration ids, never names, emails, tokens or credentials.
- CORS: only the origins in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, methods GET/POST, no credentials.
- SQL only through JPA with bound parameters (SB-05).

## §8 Frontend (US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03)

React single page as defined in `ui-contract.md`: modules `api` (fetch calls and response parsing), `validation` (client rules mirroring §4 required/email/consent/token rules), `RegistrationForm`, `OptionGroups`, `Consents`, `Captcha` (test checkbox or Google widget loaded with `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js?render=explicit`), `Confirmation`. All server text is rendered as React text (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, SB-05). Only relative `/api` URLs (AR-01).

+- Workbook (`.xlsx`, POI `XSSFWorkbook`), sheet `Registrations`, header row then one row per registration ordered by `registeredAt` (AC-008-01). Columns: `Registration ID`, `Type` (`EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT`), `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC), `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities` (selected option names of that category joined by `; `), `Consents` (`<id> (<givenAt>)` joined by `; `). Every cell is a string cell, so text is unchanged (NFR-01, AC-008-03) and never evaluated as a formula. Only registration data (SR-07).

+- Spring Security: stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies or sessions are used; the only authenticated call is a read with Basic credentials). Permit `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness`; export as §6; everything else denied (403). Actuator exposes `health` only, without details.

+- Headers on every backend response (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

+- Frontend nginx headers (SB-10): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; `client_max_body_size 16k`; `server_tokens off`; `proxy_set_header Host $proxy_host` (SR-08).

+- Rate limit (SR-03, SB-06): servlet filter before Spring Security, fixed one-minute window per (client IP, group) with the limits of §3; over the limit → 429 `{"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}` with `Retry-After`. Client IP is `request.getRemoteAddr()` after Tomcat's `RemoteIpValve` (`server.forward-headers-strategy: native`, trusting only private and loopback proxy addresses).
+- Body size (SR-03): filter rejects a declared or actual body above the limit with 413 `{"message":"Request too large."}`.

+- Errors (SB-07, ES-07): one `@RestControllerAdvice`; unexpected exceptions → 500 `{"message":"An unexpected error occurred."}`; `server.error.include-*` never; logs carry registration ids, never names, emails, tokens or credentials.
+- CORS: only the origins in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, methods GET/POST, no credentials.
+- SQL only through JPA with bound parameters (SB-05).

+React single page as defined in `ui-contract.md`: modules `api` (fetch calls and response parsing), `validation` (client rules mirroring §4 required/email/consent/token rules), `RegistrationForm`, `OptionGroups`, `Consents`, `Captcha` (test checkbox or Google widget loaded with `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js?render=explicit`), `Confirmation`. entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

### Self-check before the freeze (skill step 5)

- Timestamps from PostgreSQL are read as \`java.sql.Timestamp\` and converted explicitly (\`StorageAcceptanceTest.instant\`).
- Workbook and attachment checks compare text values or parsed JSON trees, not byte sequences; the e2e workbook reader unzips the file and decodes XML entities.

- Rejection checks first assert the status, then "nothing stored" (rows, copies, emails), so they cannot pass on an empty database alone.
- AC-008-04 contains a control request from localhost that must succeed, so the refusal cannot come from the credentials.

- Cross-test email leakage is avoided because the specification sends emails within the request, after commit (spec §4 step 7); every test resets database, copies and Mailpit first.
- Frontend tests address elements only by role, label and the \`data-testid\` values of \`ui-contract.md\`.
- All tests are formatted (Spotless, Prettier) and lint-clean (ESLint) before the freeze.

<FindBugsFilter
    xmlns="https://github.com/spotbugs/filter/3.0.0"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:schemaLocation="https://github.com/spotbugs/filter/3.0.0 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotbugs/spotbugs/3.1.0/spotbugs/etc/findbugsfilter.xsd">
  <!-- Records and JSON DTOs carry lists by design; collaborators are injected by Spring. -->
  <Match>

  </Match>
  <!-- Spring singletons validate configuration in the constructor to stop start-up (ES-01). -->
  <Match>

  </Match>
</FindBugsFilter>

# Email contract (SMTP)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03 · Agent: writes

Both emails are sent after the database transaction (with the JSON copy) has committed, after the 201 answer has been decided, by the backend through the configured SMTP server (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, optional `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`). Connection and read timeouts are 5 s. A failure of either email is logged as `Email <kind> for registration <id> failed` with no personal data and does not change the API answer (OQ-03).

## Common rules (SR-05)

- `From`: `MAIL_FROM` (setting, default `registration@konferenca.local`).
- Content: `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` only, no HTML part. User input appears only in the body, so markup is literal text.
- Headers never contain user input: the subject is built from `CONFERENCE_NAME` only; recipients are addresses that passed the email rule (no whitespace, so no CR/LF) or configured organizer addresses; no display names.
- Exactly one recipient per message in `To`; no `Cc` or `Bcc`.

## Participant confirmation (US-006, AC-006-01, AC-006-02)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email (trimmed) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmation – <CONFERENCE_NAME>` |
| Body | lines, in order: `Dear <firstName> <lastName>,` · blank · `your registration for <CONFERENCE_NAME> has been received.` · blank · `Registration ID: <id>` · `Registration type: External participant` or `Student` · blank · `Selected options:` · one line `- <option name> (<Workshop|Event|Meal|Other activity>)` per selected option, or `- none` · blank · `Kind regards,` · `<CONFERENCE_NAME> organizers` |

## Organizer notification (US-007, AC-007-01, AC-007-02, SR-07)

One message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, each trimmed and validated at start-up; an invalid address stops start-up).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | one organizer address |
| Subject | `New registration – <CONFERENCE_NAME>` |
| Body | `A new registration was received.` · blank · then one `Label: value` line each for `Registration ID`, `Registration type`, `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC), `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, and either `Organization / institution` or `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID` · blank · `Selected options:` with lines as in the participant email · blank · `Consents:` with one line `- <consent id>: given at <ISO-8601 UTC>` per consent |
| Attachment | `registration-<id>.json`, content type `application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`) |

Only registration data appears (SR-07): no internal ids other than the registration id, no configuration values, no server information.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable list, give the mandatory consent and pass Google reCAPTCHA v2. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, the participant gets a confirmation email, every organizer gets a notification with the JSON attached, and organizers can download all registrations as an Excel workbook.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4 REST API under `/api` (Java 21, PostgreSQL, Flyway, SMTP, Apache POI) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page (Vite, TypeScript), served by nginx, proxies `/api` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |

The local stack in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) runs both with PostgreSQL 16 and the Mailpit mail catcher.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, JDK 21 (only to build the backend jar), Node.js 24 with npm 11 (only for frontend development and tests). Versions: [`01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`](../01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md).

1. At the repository root, copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` and fill `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. `.env` is ignored by git.
2. Build the backend jar:

   ```sh
   cd 02_output/backend
   ./mvnw -B package -DskipTests
   ```

3. Start the stack from `02_output/`:

   ```sh
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   ```

4. Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080> for the registration form and <http://127.0.0.1:8025> for the emails caught by Mailpit. The local stack runs reCAPTCHA in test mode (a "I am not a robot (test mode)" checkbox).
5. Export as organizer: `curl -u "<ORGANIZER_USERNAME>:<ORGANIZER_PASSWORD>" -o registrations.xlsx http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations/export`.
6. Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; data stays in the volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes it).

End-to-end tests against the running stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#test).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, configuration, behaviour, security design, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, JSON schemas, shipped options configuration, database schema, email and UI contracts |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, frozen tests, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition-of-done evidence, runtime demonstration, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests, data retention |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision taken during the run |

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API of the conference registration (`docs/02_contracts/openapi.yaml`): form configuration, registration with reCAPTCHA verification, storage in PostgreSQL plus a JSON copy, emails, and the organizer Excel export. Architecture: ports and adapters, root package `si.konferenca.registration` (spec §2, checked by `ArchitectureTest`).

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (Temurin 21.0.10 pinned; the runtime image is `eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7-jre-alpine`). Maven itself is downloaded by the wrapper (`./mvnw`, Maven 3.9.9).
- Docker for the tests (Testcontainers starts `postgres:16.15-alpine` and `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1`) and for the container image.

## Configuration

All settings come from environment variables (spec §3). Entries without a default are required; the backend does not start without them.

| Variable | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USERNAME` | none | environment (compose sets them locally) |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none | secret, `.env` |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` | none | environment (Mailpit locally) |
| `SMTP_STARTTLS` | `true` | environment (`false` for Mailpit) |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty | secret, production only |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.local` | environment |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none | secret, `.env` (comma separated) |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none | secret, `.env`; password ≥ 16 characters, kept only as a BCrypt hash |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | environment; `false` only on local plain HTTP |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | environment |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | none | location of the options file, e.g. `file:/config/conference.json`; shipped file: [config/conference.json](config/conference.json), schema `docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json` |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `/data/json-copies` | environment (persistent volume) |
| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | environment; `true` only for test and local |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | secret, production only |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | environment |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | empty | local Vite dev server only |
| `RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG_PER_MINUTE`, `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATIONS_PER_MINUTE`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_MINUTE` | 60, 10, 10 | environment |
| `REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | 16384 | environment |
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | none | `prod` in production: start-up fails with test mode on, empty reCAPTCHA keys or HTTPS-only off |

Changing the offered options: edit the options file and restart; an invalid file stops start-up with a message naming the problem.

## Build

```sh
./mvnw -B package -DskipTests        # target/registration-backend-0.1.0.jar
docker build -t registration-backend .   # after the jar exists
```

## Run

Locally the backend runs in the compose stack (root README). To run the jar directly, export the required variables above, then `java -jar target/registration-backend-0.1.0.jar`. Health: `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness`.

## Test

```sh
./mvnw -B verify                     # all 203 tests: unit, integration, architecture, acceptance (Docker needed)
./mvnw -B spotless:check pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check   # check: format, lint, static analysis
./mvnw -B spotless:apply             # format
./mvnw -B jacoco:report              # coverage report after a test run (target/site/jacoco)
./mvnw -B org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage   # mutation testing (about 15 minutes)
```

Dependency scan (needs `NVD_API_KEY` exported from `.env`): `./mvnw -B org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0:check`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `Could not resolve placeholder 'DATABASE_URL'` (or another variable) at start-up | a required variable is missing; set it |
| `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD must have at least 16 characters` | use a longer organizer password in `.env` |

# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React single page of the conference registration (`docs/02_contracts/ui-contract.md`). It talks to the backend only through relative `/api` URLs and holds no secret; the reCAPTCHA site key comes from `GET /api/form-config`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13.0 with npm 11.6.2.
- For end-to-end tests: Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium`, once) and the running local stack.

## Configuration

The built page has no settings of its own. Behaviour that differs per environment comes from the backend (`captcha.mode`, `captcha.siteKey`, conference name, options). The container's nginx ([nginx.conf](nginx.conf)) serves the page on port 8080, sets the security headers and proxies `/api/` to `http://backend:8080` with its own `Host` header. The dev server (`npm run dev`) proxies `/api` to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`.

## Build

```sh
npm ci
npm run build                      # type check + production bundle in dist/
docker build -t registration-frontend .
```

## Run

```sh
npm run dev                        # http://127.0.0.1:5173, needs a backend on 127.0.0.1:8080
```

In the local stack the frontend runs as a container on <http://127.0.0.1:8080> (root README).

## Test

```sh
npm test                           # Vitest: unit and acceptance tests (56)
npm run check                      # Prettier, ESLint, tsc --noEmit
npm run coverage                   # coverage report in coverage/
npm run mutation                   # Stryker mutation testing (about 5 minutes)
npm run duplication                # jscpd
```

End-to-end tests (Playwright, against the running stack from the root README). They read the organizer credentials from the environment, so export them from `.env` without printing them:

```sh
export ORGANIZER_USERNAME="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
export ORGANIZER_PASSWORD="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
npm run e2e
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| "The registration form is currently unavailable" | `/api/form-config` failed; check that the backend is healthy (`docker compose ps`) |
| e2e: `ORGANIZER_USERNAME and ORGANIZER_PASSWORD must be exported from .env` | export them as shown above |
| e2e: Mailpit or `docker compose exec` errors | start the stack first; Mailpit must listen on 127.0.0.1:8025 |
| e2e: HTTP 429 | the stack allows 10 registrations per minute per client; wait a minute and re-run |
| `npx playwright` cannot find Chromium | run `npx playwright install chromium` |

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable list, give the mandatory consent and pass Google reCAPTCHA v2. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, the participant gets a confirmation email, every organizer gets a notification with the JSON attached, and organizers can download all registrations as an Excel workbook.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4 REST API under `/api` (Java 21, PostgreSQL, Flyway, SMTP, Apache POI) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page (Vite, TypeScript), served by nginx, proxies `/api` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |

The local stack in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) runs both with PostgreSQL 16 and the Mailpit mail catcher.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, JDK 21 (only to build the backend jar), Node.js 24 with npm 11 (only for frontend development and tests). Versions: [`01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`](../01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md).

1. At the repository root, copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` and fill `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. `.env` is ignored by git.
2. Build the backend jar:

   ```sh
   cd 02_output/backend
   ./mvnw -B package -DskipTests
   ```

3. Start the stack from `02_output/`:

   ```sh
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   ```

4. Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080> for the registration form and <http://127.0.0.1:8025> for the emails caught by Mailpit. The local stack runs reCAPTCHA in test mode (a "I am not a robot (test mode)" checkbox).
5. Export as organizer: `curl -u "<ORGANIZER_USERNAME>:<ORGANIZER_PASSWORD>" -o registrations.xlsx http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations/export`.
6. Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; data stays in the volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes it).

End-to-end tests against the running stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#test).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, configuration, behaviour, security design, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, JSON schemas, shipped options configuration, database schema, email and UI contracts |

| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests, data retention |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision taken during the run |

# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Agent: writes

Version 0.1.0 of the conference registration (backend `registration-backend` 0.1.0, frontend `registration-frontend` 0.1.0).

## Delivered

- US-001, US-002: registration forms for external participants and students, client and server validation, Unicode text (č, š, ž), reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the backend.
- US-003: options (workshops, events, meals, other activities) and consents from a JSON configuration file, per-type availability, refused start-up on an invalid file.
- US-004: in-application confirmation only after acceptance; field errors next to the fields; general error without technical details.
- US-005: every accepted registration in PostgreSQL and as `<id>.json` on a persistent volume, written in one transaction.
- US-006, US-007: plain-text participant confirmation and organizer notification with the JSON copy attached; a mail failure does not lose the registration.
- US-008: Excel export for the organizer (HTTP Basic, HTTPS-only outside localhost).
- Security: rate and size limits, security headers, non-root containers, production safety check (`SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod`).
- Quality: 35/35 acceptance criteria covered by frozen tests; backend 203 tests, line coverage 98.19 %, mutation score 90.54 %; frontend 56 tests plus 5 end-to-end, line coverage 100 %, mutation score 92.58 % (`docs/03_test-strategy.md`).

## Data retention (OQ-06)

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable list, give the mandatory consent and pass Google reCAPTCHA v2. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, the participant gets a confirmation email, every organizer gets a notification with the JSON attached, and organizers can download all registrations as an Excel workbook.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4 REST API under `/api` (Java 21, PostgreSQL, Flyway, SMTP, Apache POI) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page (Vite, TypeScript), served by nginx, proxies `/api` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |

The local stack in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) runs both with PostgreSQL 16 and the Mailpit mail catcher.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, JDK 21 (only to build the backend jar), Node.js 24 with npm 11 (only for frontend development and tests). Versions: [`01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`](../01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md).

1. At the repository root, copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` and fill `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. `.env` is ignored by git.
2. Build the backend jar:

   ```sh
   cd 02_output/backend
   ./mvnw -B package -DskipTests
   ```

3. Start the stack from `02_output/`:

   ```sh
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   ```

4. Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080> for the registration form and <http://127.0.0.1:8025> for the emails caught by Mailpit. The local stack runs reCAPTCHA in test mode (a "I am not a robot (test mode)" checkbox).
5. Export as organizer: `curl -u "<ORGANIZER_USERNAME>:<ORGANIZER_PASSWORD>" -o registrations.xlsx http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations/export`.
6. Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; data stays in the volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes it).

End-to-end tests against the running stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#test).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, configuration, behaviour, security design, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, JSON schemas, shipped options configuration, database schema, email and UI contracts |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, frozen tests, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition-of-done evidence, runtime demonstration, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests, data retention |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision taken during the run |
